title: Bell says it's investigating cyberattack that led to potential theft of business customer data
summary: Bell says it's investigating a cyber incident in which some enterprise client data may have been stolen. A spokesperson confirmed an "agentic" threat actor was able to access some of the company's…

image.caption: A Bell store in downtown Montreal pictured in May 2025. The company says it is investigating the theft of some business client data earlier this week. (Christopher Katsarov/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Bell says it's investigating a cyber incident in which some enterprise client data may have been stolen. A spokesperson confirmed an "agentic" threat actor was able to access some of the company's systems, including one used for ordering and supplying telecommunication networks.
Company says it was able to quickly contain 'agentic' attack on Tuesday
Bell says it's investigating a cyber incident in which some enterprise client data may have been stolen.
A Bell spokesperson confirmed with CBC News that an "agentic" threat actor was able to access some of the company's systems, including one used for ordering and supplying telecommunication networks.

Some client data, including business contact information like names, corporate email addresses, phone numbers, as well as IP addresses, were stolen in the attack, the company says. Its investigation has so far determined that things like files and PDFs, which would contain more sensitive information, were not affected.
Bell says it was quickly able to contain the threat in the attack, which took place on Tuesday.

"Upon learning of the breach, we immediately contained the incident and secured our systems. There has been no impact to customer services," public affairs manager Zoe Chapman said in an emailed statement. Bell said it is reaching out to affected customers directly.
The company says it's unclear at this point who the perpetrator is, as nobody has contacted the company claiming responsibility.

items: KPMG Canada client documents accessed in cybersecurity breach, accounting firm says

blocks.text: The telecom firm also says it has shared "indicators of compromise" — essentially, digital footprints that give evidence of an attack — with enterprise customers and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (CCCS). It's also reached out to the RCMP’s cybercrime unit and is pursuing its own investigation into the matter.

The incident comes after a string of cyberattacks targeting legal and financial firms in Canada through voice phishing ("vishing") scams, in which fraudulent phone numbers and voice-altering software can be used to contact potential victims by phone.
KPMG Canada confirmed earlier this week some of its clients' tax documents had been accessed in a breach, while four major law firms were targeted by a similar vishing incident in October.
